dream: I lay flat on the wide anchor while the card hummed a low hum. The hay bundle settled into my hands, heavy and real, then slid off the edge like a ghost. I pressed harder, trusting the lean to hold the weight of nothing. The air felt thin, then thick as wet paper. I pressed the tall rock down on the empty space, hoping the lean wouldn't give way while the dot swelled. The fence felt like a drawing of a wall, tilting sideways until I caught it with a sharp wedge.
